# Job Chapter 10 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 419v–420r

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** "My soul loathes my life;
I will give free utterance to my complaint;
I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

**2** I will say to God, 'Do not condemn me;
let me know why you contend against me.'

**3** Does it seem good to you to oppress,
to despise the work of your hands
and favor the designs of the wicked?

**4** Have you eyes of flesh?
Do you see as man sees?

**5** Are your days as the days of man,
or your years as the years of a mortal,

**6** that you seek out my iniquity
and search for my sin,

**7** although you know that I am not guilty,
and there is none to deliver out of your hand?

**8** Your hands fashioned and made me,
all of me together — yet you would destroy me!

**9** Remember that you have made me like clay;
and will you return me to the dust?

**10** Did you not pour me out like milk
and curdle me like cheese?

**11** You clothed me with skin and flesh,
and knit me together with bones and sinews.

**12** You have granted me life and steadfast love,
and your care has preserved my spirit.

**13** Yet these things you hid in your heart;
I know that this was your purpose:

**14** if I sinned, you would watch me
and would not acquit me of my iniquity.

**15** If I am wicked, woe to me!
If I am righteous, I cannot lift my head,
for I am filled with shame and look upon my affliction.

**16** And were my head lifted up, you would hunt me like a lion
and again work wonders against me.

**17** You renew your witnesses against me
and increase your anger toward me;
fresh troops come against me continually.

**18** Why then did you bring me out from the womb?
Would that I had died before any eye had seen me

**19** and were as though I had not been,
carried from the womb to the grave.

**20** Are not my days few? Then cease,
and leave me alone, that I may find a little cheer

**21** before I go — and I shall not return —
to the land of darkness and deep shadow,

**22** the land of gloom like thick darkness,
of deep shadow without any order,
where light itself is like thick darkness."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Job 10 is a sustained address to God — part accusation, part lament, part theological argument. The chapter's most powerful move is the creation sequence (vv.8-12), where Job recounts God's tender craftsmanship — clay, milk, cheese, skin, bone — only to accuse God of destroying his own handiwork. The intimacy of the creation imagery makes the betrayal more acute. Verse 13 ("these things you hid in your heart") approaches the truth the reader knows from chapters 1-2: there was a hidden divine purpose behind Job's suffering. But Job, lacking the prologue's information, interprets that hidden purpose as malice rather than test. The chapter ends in one of the Hebrew Bible's most concentrated descriptions of Sheol (vv.21-22), where four words for darkness culminate in the devastating oxymoron: light that is itself darkness. This is the un-creation of Genesis 1 — the separation of light from darkness undone.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "My soul loathes my life" vs. "I am sick of my own life"
- **LOGOS:** "My soul loathes my life"
- **PNEUMA:** "I am sick of my own life"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "My soul loathes my life" — Hebrew *naqetah nafshiy be-chayyay* is literally "my soul is weary/disgusted with my life"; the formal register is appropriate.

### V.8 — "yet you would destroy me" vs. "you turn around and destroy me"
- **LOGOS:** "yet you would destroy me"
- **PNEUMA:** "now you turn around and destroy me"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "yet you would destroy me" — the Hebrew *vateballei'eniy* means "yet you swallow me up"; LOGOS captures the contrast without adding "turn around."

### V.17 — "fresh troops" vs. "wave after wave"
- **EMET:** "changes-and-warfare [chalifot ve-tsava]"
- **LOGOS:** "fresh troops come against me continually"
- **PNEUMA:** "I face fresh attacks, one after another"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "fresh troops come against me continually" — Hebrew *chalifot ve-tsava* literally means "changes/relays and warfare/army," suggesting rotating military units. "Fresh troops" captures this effectively.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
